questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The traditional multi-course Kashmiri wedding feast — known for its elaborate meat preparations served on the 'trami' — is called:
questions.explanation: Wazwan is the traditional Kashmiri multi-course banquet, usually 36 courses, prepared by the Wazas (master chefs) and served on a large copper platter called a trami shared by four diners. 'Rista Feast' is not a standard term; rista is only one dish (minced-meat balls in red gravy) within Wazwan. 'Sadya' is the traditional multi-course vegetarian meal of Kerala, not Kashmir. 'Tabak Maaz' is a specific fried-rib dish served during Wazwan, not the name of the feast itself.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The elegant group dance performed by Kashmiri women, standing shoulder-to-shoulder in rows and swaying with folk songs, especially during Eid and Baisakhi, is called:
questions.explanation: Rouf (also spelled Rouv/Rowuf) is the traditional Kashmiri women's group dance, performed shoulder-to-shoulder in rows to folk songs, most visibly during Eid, Ramzan and Baisakhi. 'Kud' is a Dogra folk dance of the hilly regions of Jammu, performed by men, not the women's group dance in question. 'Bhand Pather' is a folk theatre tradition of Kashmir (satirical drama), not a group dance. 'Dumhal' is a ritualistic dance of the Wattal community performed by men in tall caps carrying a banner — different from Rouf.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The traditional folk dance of the Duggar region of Jammu, performed at night around a bonfire during the harvest season, is:
questions.explanation: Kud is the traditional folk dance of the Duggar (Jammu hills) region, performed at night to thank the mountain deities after a good harvest; participants dance around a bonfire to the beats of drums and flutes. 'Bhand Pather' is Kashmiri folk theatre, not a Duggar dance. 'Rouf' is a Kashmiri women's dance, not from the Duggar region. 'Chakri' is a Kashmiri musical ensemble (folk music), not a Duggar dance form.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Bhand Pather is best described as:
options: A satirical folk theatre form of Kashmir combining dance, music and mimicry
A style of Pashmina shawl weaving practised in Kanihama
A classical Kashmiri musical genre based on Persian ragas
A traditional copper-utensil craft associated with Srinagar
questions.correctAnswer: A satirical folk theatre form of Kashmir combining dance, music and mimicry
questions.explanation: Bhand Pather is the centuries-old folk theatre tradition of Kashmir, performed by 'Bhands' who combine dance, music, satire and mimicry to comment on social and political issues. Pashmina shawl weaving is a distinct handicraft tradition, not a theatrical form. Sufiana Kalam is the classical Kashmiri musical genre inspired by Persian modes; Bhand Pather is not that genre. Copper-utensil work (kandkari) is a metal craft of Srinagar, not a form of drama.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The extremely fine wool used for the world-famous Pashmina shawls of Kashmir is obtained from the:
options: Mesta plant grown along the Chenab
Undercoat fleece of the Changthangi goat reared in Ladakh
Merino sheep bred in the Kashmir valley
Silk cocoons produced in Anantnag district
questions.correctAnswer: Undercoat fleece of the Changthangi goat reared in Ladakh
questions.explanation: Genuine Pashmina wool ('Pashm') is combed from the soft undercoat of the Changthangi goat of the Changthang plateau of Ladakh, and is then hand-spun and hand-woven in Kashmir. Mesta is a fibre crop, not a wool source. Merino sheep produce a coarser wool marketed globally as merino, not Pashmina; Pashmina specifically requires the Changthangi goat. Silk from cocoons is used for sericulture products, not for Pashmina shawls.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following Kashmiri products received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag primarily to protect its origin and authenticity from imitations?
questions.explanation: Kashmiri Pashmina holds a GI tag identifying it as a specialty product of Jammu & Kashmir, protecting the name from imitation by machine-made or synthetic-blend shawls. Punjabi Phulkari is a GI product of Punjab (not J&K). Banarasi Silk Saree is a GI product of Uttar Pradesh (Varanasi). Chikan Embroidery of Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh) also has its own GI tag — none of these three are Kashmiri products, so they do not fit the 'Kashmiri product' criterion.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into effect on:
questions.explanation: The Act was enacted in August 2019, but its 'appointed day' — the day on which the erstwhile State of Jammu & Kashmir formally became two Union Territories (J&K and Ladakh) — was 31 October 2019 (chosen to coincide with the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, National Unity Day). '15 August 2019' is Independence Day and is unrelated. '5 August 2019' is the day of the Presidential order and parliamentary resolutions on Article 370, not the reorganisation appointed day. '26 January 2020' is Republic Day of 2020, unrelated to the reorganisation appointed day.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: As per the Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (post-delimitation position), the total number of districts in the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir is:
questions.explanation: The Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir has 20 districts — 10 in the Jammu division (Jammu, Kathua, Samba, Udhampur, Reasi, Doda, Kishtwar, Ramban, Poonch, Rajouri) and 10 in the Kashmir division (Srinagar, Ganderbal, Budgam, Anantnag, Kulgam, Pulwama, Shopian, Baramulla, Bandipora, Kupwara). '10' refers only to one of the two divisions, not the whole UT. '16' was an interim figure before 2007 and is outdated. '22' overshoots by two and does not match the current administrative count.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: After the 2022 delimitation exercise, the total number of Legislative Assembly seats (excluding nominated members) in the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir is:
questions.explanation: The Delimitation Commission's final order (May 2022) fixed the strength of the J&K Legislative Assembly at 90 elected seats (43 in Jammu division and 47 in Kashmir division). '76' was the number of seats in the erstwhile State assembly excluding the 24 reserved for PoK. '83' was the pre-delimitation elected strength before adjustments. '87' was the total elected strength of the pre-2019 J&K State Assembly (excluding PoK seats); after reorganisation and delimitation this changed to 90.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The common High Court that has territorial jurisdiction over the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir and the Union Territory of Ladakh is:
options: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh
The Supreme Court of Jammu Division
questions.correctAnswer: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh
questions.explanation: After the 2019 reorganisation, the erstwhile J&K High Court was renamed the 'High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh' with two seats (Srinagar and Jammu); it has jurisdiction over both UTs. 'High Court of Kashmir' and 'High Court of Ladakh' are not names of any actual court. There is no such body as the 'Supreme Court of Jammu Division' — the Supreme Court is a single body located in New Delhi for the whole country.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir (following the 2019 reorganisation) was:
questions.explanation: Girish Chandra (G.C.) Murmu was sworn in on 31 October 2019 as the first LG of the newly-formed UT of Jammu & Kashmir. N.N. Vohra was the last Governor of the erstwhile State of J&K (before UT status). Satya Pal Malik was the Governor of J&K just before Vohra's departure and at the time of the reorganisation announcement — he was Governor of the STATE, not LG of the UT. Manoj Sinha is the second and current LG (appointed in August 2020), not the first.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In the horticulture sector of Jammu & Kashmir, the largest single fruit crop by area and production is:
questions.explanation: Apple is by far the leading fruit crop of J&K in both area under cultivation and total production; J&K produces the bulk of India's apples and the crop is central to the UT's rural economy (with Sopore, Shopian and Kulgam being major centres). Cherry is a niche high-value crop with far smaller acreage. Walnut is a significant crop (India's walnut supply is dominated by J&K), but it is grown on a much smaller area than apple. Pear is grown on a small area as well and does not approach apple in either area or output.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Kashmiri language is officially written today in the __________ script.
questions.explanation: In modern use — including school textbooks, newspapers, government publications and the Jammu & Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020 — Kashmiri is written in the Perso-Arabic script (Nastaʿlīq style). 'Devanagari' is sometimes used academically but is not the primary official script. 'Sharada' is the ancient script of Kashmir, now used only ceremonially by Kashmiri Pandits — not the modern official script. 'Roman' is used only informally on the internet and has no official status.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Under the Jammu & Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020, which of the following is NOT among the five official languages of the UT of J&K?
questions.explanation: The 2020 Act notified five official languages for the UT of J&K: Kashmiri, Dogri, Urdu, Hindi and English. Punjabi is widely spoken in parts of Jammu but was NOT included among the five official languages of J&K under this Act. Urdu is included (it was earlier the sole official language of the State). Kashmiri is included (added after long civil-society demand). Dogri is included, reflecting its importance in Jammu division.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019:

(i) It bifurcated the State of Jammu & Kashmir into two Union Territories — J&K and Ladakh.
(ii) The Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir has a Legislative Assembly, while the Union Territory of Ladakh does not have a Legislative Assembly.
(iii) After the Act, the executive head of each UT is a Chief Minister and the constitutional head is the Governor.
(iv) The 'appointed day' notified for the reorganisation was 31 October 2019.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i), (ii) and (iv) are all correct facts about the reorganisation. Statement (iii) is FALSE — a Union Territory does NOT have a Governor; its constitutional head is a Lieutenant Governor (LG). Also, Ladakh being without an Assembly, there is no Chief Minister for that UT. Any option including (iii) is therefore wrong: '(i), (iii) and (iv) only' drops the true (ii) and keeps false (iii); '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' drops the true (i) and keeps (iii); 'All of the above' wrongly accepts (iii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the current administrative structure of the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) It has a Lieutenant Governor as the constitutional head.
(ii) The UT is divided into two administrative divisions — Jammu division and Kashmir division.
(iii) The UT of Ladakh has an elected Legislative Assembly of its own.
(iv) The Common High Court has its seats at Srinagar and Jammu.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct — the UT has an LG, is administered through two divisions (Jammu and Kashmir), and its Common High Court has seats at both Srinagar and Jammu (with the Darbar Move earlier alternating locations). Statement (iii) is FALSE — Ladakh is a UT WITHOUT a Legislative Assembly; it is administered directly through the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils and the LG. Any option including (iii) is therefore wrong: '(i), (ii) and (iii) only' includes false (iii); '(i), (iii) and (iv) only' includes (iii) and drops true (ii); 'All of the above' wrongly accepts (iii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Wazwan:

(i) It is traditionally cooked by chefs called 'Wazas'.
(ii) It is served on a large copper platter (trami) shared by four persons.
(iii) The full Wazwan is a purely vegetarian meal with no meat courses.
(iv) Rista, Rogan Josh, Gushtaba and Tabak Maaz are among its well-known courses.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct — Wazwan is prepared by Wazas, served on a shared trami, and its signature dishes include Rista, Rogan Josh, Gushtaba and Tabak Maaz. Statement (iii) is FALSE — Wazwan is famous precisely because it is a meat-heavy multi-course feast with a large number of lamb / mutton preparations. Any option including (iii) is therefore wrong: '(i), (ii) and (iii) only' includes false (iii) and drops true (iv); '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' keeps (iii) and drops true (i); '(i), (iii) and (iv) only' keeps (iii) and drops true (ii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the handicrafts of Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) Papier-mâché is a traditional decorative craft strongly associated with Srinagar.
(ii) Kani shawls are hand-woven on small wooden sticks called kanis, mainly in the Kanihama area.
(iii) Walnut wood carving is an important wood-craft of the Kashmir valley.
(iv) Basohli painting is a delicate metal-inlay craft native to the Kashmir valley.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i), (ii) and (iii) correctly describe well-known crafts. Statement (iv) is FALSE — Basohli is a school of MINIATURE PAINTING (not metal inlay) associated with Basohli in the Jammu region, NOT with the Kashmir valley. Any option including (iv) is therefore wrong: '(i), (ii) and (iv) only' includes false (iv) and drops true (iii); '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' includes (iv) and drops true (i); '(i), (iii) and (iv) only' includes (iv) and drops true (ii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the culture of Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) Sheikh Nooruddin Wali (Nund Rishi) is regarded as the patron saint of Kashmir and a founder of the Rishi Order.
(ii) Lal Ded (Lalleshwari) was a 14th-century Kashmiri Shaivite mystic and poetess.
(iii) Kahwa is a traditional Kashmiri green tea often flavoured with cardamom, saffron and almonds.
(iv) The Kashmiri script known as Sharada is used today in all official government publications of the UT.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct standard facts. Statement (iv) is FALSE — Sharada is an ancient historical script, no longer used for everyday or official Kashmiri; the current official script is Perso-Arabic (Nastaʿlīq). Any option including (iv) is therefore wrong: '(i), (ii) and (iv) only' drops the true (iii) and keeps false (iv); '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' drops the true (i) and keeps (iv); 'All of the above' wrongly accepts (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Saffron cultivation of very high quality is possible in the Pampore area of Pulwama district.
Reason (R): Saffron requires a well-drained calcareous 'karewa' soil and a cool, dry autumn — conditions which the Pampore plateau naturally provides.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is a well-established fact about the Kashmir saffron belt. (R) is scientifically correct — saffron (Crocus sativus) needs karewa (elevated, well-drained calcareous silt) and a cool, dry flowering season, both characteristic of the Pampore plateau. (R) directly explains (A). The second option is wrong because (R) does explain (A). The third and fourth options are wrong because both statements are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Union Territory of Ladakh does not participate in any elections to its own Legislative Assembly.
Reason (R): The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 constituted Ladakh as a Union Territory without a Legislative Assembly.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Ladakh does not have any Assembly of its own, so no Assembly elections are held there (its representative democracy operates through the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils and a single Lok Sabha seat). (R) is a correct statement of law under the 2019 Act, and it directly explains (A). The second option is wrong because (R) does explain (A). Options three and four are wrong because both (A) and (R) are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the UT of Jammu & Kashmir, the Chief Minister is the constitutional head of the Union Territory.
Reason (R): The Lieutenant Governor of a UT is appointed by the President of India.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: (A) is FALSE — in a UT with a Legislative Assembly, the CONSTITUTIONAL head is the Lieutenant Governor, not the Chief Minister; the CM is only the head of the elected government (council of ministers). (R) is correct — the LG of every UT is appointed by the President of India. So the correct choice is 'A is not correct but R is correct'. The first two options require (A) to be correct, which it is not. The third option is wrong because (R) is a correct statement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following folk performance forms in Column I with the region / community best associated with them in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Rouf
(b) Kud
(c) Bhand Pather
(d) Dumhal

Column II:
(i) Wattal community of Kashmir (men in tall caps carrying a banner)
(ii) Duggar (Jammu hills) — men dancing around a bonfire
(iii) Kashmir valley — women's group dance in rows
(iv) Kashmir valley — folk theatre with dance, music and satire

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Rouf is the women's group dance of Kashmir → (a)-(iii). Kud is the Duggar men's dance around a bonfire → (b)-(ii). Bhand Pather is Kashmiri folk theatre → (c)-(iv). Dumhal is performed by the Wattal community with tall caps and banner → (d)-(i). The second option wrongly pairs Rouf with folk theatre. The third option pairs Bhand Pather with the Wattal community, which is Dumhal's association, not Bhand Pather's. The fourth option pairs Rouf with the Duggar dance, which is Kud, not Rouf.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following crafts in Column I with the correct description in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Pashmina shawl
(b) Kani shawl
(c) Papier-mâché
(d) Walnut wood carving

Column II:
(i) Woven on small wooden sticks (kanis), traditionally in the Kanihama area
(ii) Fine wool shawl from the fleece of the Changthangi goat of Ladakh
(iii) Intricate wood-craft associated with the Kashmir valley
(iv) Lacquered paper craft, especially of Srinagar, used to make boxes, pen-stands and decorations

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Pashmina uses the Changthangi goat's fleece → (a)-(ii). Kani shawls are woven on small wooden 'kani' sticks → (b)-(i). Papier-mâché is the lacquered paper craft of Srinagar → (c)-(iv). Walnut wood carving is a distinct woodcraft of the Kashmir valley → (d)-(iii). The first option swaps Pashmina and Kani. The third option pairs Kani with papier-mâché and vice-versa. The fourth option pairs Pashmina with papier-mâché — obvious mismatch.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following hydroelectric projects in Column I with the river on which each is built in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Salal Hydroelectric Project
(b) Baglihar Hydroelectric Project
(c) Uri Hydroelectric Project
(d) Kishenganga Hydroelectric Project

Column II:
(i) Jhelum
(ii) Chenab
(iii) Kishenganga (Neelam)
(iv) Chenab

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Salal is on the Chenab → (a)-(ii). Baglihar is also on the Chenab → (b)-(iv). Uri is on the Jhelum → (c)-(i). Kishenganga is on the Kishenganga (Neelam) river → (d)-(iii). The second option puts Salal on the Jhelum, which is wrong (Uri is on Jhelum, not Salal). The third option places Salal on the Kishenganga and Kishenganga on the Jhelum — both wrong. The fourth option pairs Salal with Kishenganga and Kishenganga with Chenab — both wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are recognised folk dance / theatre forms native to Jammu & Kashmir?

(i) Kud
(ii) Rouf
(iii) Bhand Pather
(iv) Garba

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Kud, Rouf and Bhand Pather are all traditional performance forms of J&K. Garba is a folk dance of Gujarat, not of Jammu & Kashmir. Any option that includes Garba (iv) is therefore wrong: '(i), (ii) and (iv) only' drops Bhand Pather (a genuine J&K form) and adds Garba; '(i), (iii) and (iv) only' drops Rouf and adds Garba; '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' drops Kud and adds Garba. Only '(i), (ii) and (iii) only' picks precisely the J&K forms.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are famous Mughal gardens located in Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir)?

(i) Shalimar Bagh
(ii) Nishat Bagh
(iii) Chashme Shahi
(iv) Buland Bagh

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh (built by Jahangir), Nishat Bagh (built by Asaf Khan) and Chashme Shahi (built during Shah Jahan's reign) are the three famous Mughal gardens on the shores of Dal Lake in Srinagar. 'Buland Bagh' is not a Mughal garden in Srinagar; the name does not correspond to any historical Mughal garden of Kashmir. Any option that includes (iv) is therefore wrong: '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' includes false (iv) and drops true (i); '(i), (iii) and (iv) only' drops true (ii) and includes (iv); '(i), (ii) and (iv) only' drops true (iii) and includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct about the present administrative structure of the UT of Jammu & Kashmir?

(i) The Lieutenant Governor is appointed by the President of India.
(ii) There are two administrative divisions — Jammu division and Kashmir division.
(iii) The Legislative Assembly (elected) has 90 seats after 2022 delimitation.
(iv) The Chief Justice of India directly presides over the High Court seats at Srinagar and Jammu.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i), (ii) and (iii) correctly describe the current setup. Statement (iv) is FALSE — the Chief Justice of India presides over the Supreme Court, not the High Court of J&K and Ladakh; the High Court is headed by its own Chief Justice. Any option including (iv) is therefore wrong: '(i), (ii) and (iv) only' includes false (iv) and drops true (iii); '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' drops true (i) and keeps (iv); 'All of the above' wrongly accepts (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 14th-century Kashmiri Shaivite mystic and poetess famous for her 'Vakhs' (verse-sayings) was __________.
questions.explanation: Lal Ded (also called Lalleshwari or Lalla-Ded), 14th century, is the celebrated Kashmiri Shaivite mystic-poetess whose short verse-sayings called 'Vakhs' are foundational to Kashmiri literature. Habba Khatoon (16th c.) was a great Kashmiri lyric poet-queen, associated with Sultan Yousuf Shah Chak — different era and different genre. Rupa Bhawani was a 17th-century Kashmiri Shaivite saint-poetess — later than Lal Ded. Arnimal was an 18th-century Kashmiri poet — even later, and famous for love poetry, not for Vakhs.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows the approximate share of major fruit crops in the total fruit production of Jammu & Kashmir (illustrative, hypothetical percentages):

Crop : Share of J&K fruit production
Apple : 70%
Walnut : 10%
Pear : 8%
Cherry : 4%
Others : 8%

Which of the following inferences is BEST supported by the above data?
options: Walnut and pear together contribute a larger share than apple
Cherry is the second-largest fruit crop by share in J&K's fruit production
Apple alone accounts for more than two-thirds of J&K's total fruit production by weight
Apple contributes less than half of J&K's total fruit production
questions.correctAnswer: Apple alone accounts for more than two-thirds of J&K's total fruit production by weight
questions.explanation: 70% > 66.67% (= 2/3), so apple alone contributes MORE than two-thirds — supported by the data. 'Cherry is the second-largest' is wrong; cherry is at 4% while walnut is at 10%, so walnut is the second-largest. 'Walnut and pear together contribute a larger share than apple' is wrong; walnut + pear = 10% + 8% = 18%, well below apple's 70%. 'Apple contributes less than half of J&K's total fruit production' is directly contradicted by the 70% figure.
